name: e-indep
summary: Four conversions that have nothing to do with each other. The control for Task C, whose four slices call each other in a chain.

slices.implement: `roman` is unimplemented. Implement it so its tests pass. It converts 1 to 3999 into Roman numerals, with the usual subtractive pairs; anything outside that range gives an empty string.
slices.specify: `roman(n: u32) -> String` converts 1 to 3999 into Roman numerals, using the subtractive pairs IV, IX, XL, XC, CD and CM. A number outside that range gives an empty string.

slices.implement: `wrap` is unimplemented. Implement it so its tests pass. It is a greedy word wrap: words are whatever lies between runs of whitespace, a line never exceeds the width, and a word longer than the width gets a line to itself rather than being split.
slices.specify: `wrap(text: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String>` wraps text greedily. Words are whatever lies between runs of whitespace, a line never exceeds `width` characters, and a word longer than `width` gets a line to itself rather than being split.

slices.implement: `base32` is unimplemented. Implement it so its tests pass. It is RFC 4648 base32: the alphabet A-Z then 2-7, five bytes to eight characters, padded with '=' to a multiple of eight.
slices.specify: `base32(bytes: &[u8]) -> String` encodes bytes as RFC 4648 base32: the alphabet A-Z followed by 2-7, five input bytes to eight output characters, padded with '=' to a multiple of eight.

slices.implement: `luhn` is unimplemented. Implement it so its tests pass. It is the Luhn checksum. Spaces may appear anywhere and are ignored; any other character makes the input invalid, as does fewer than two digits.
slices.specify: `luhn(digits: &str) -> bool` is the Luhn checksum. Spaces may appear anywhere and are ignored; any other character makes the input invalid, as does fewer than two digits.
